label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Sizwe, breathe boet. Mechanic here, I run a workshop in Umbilo. First thing: take the key out and put it in your pocket. Do NOT crank it again and do NOT put diesel in.

Kobus means well, but that's old Land Rover advice. Your D-Max is common rail and it can't take it. The pump gets its lubrication from the diesel, and petrol has none, so every time that engine turns over the pump is running dry. Diesel on top won't fix it either. The petrol is still in there and mixing does nothing.

Straight answer on the damage: it ran, stalled, and got cranked 5 or 6 times, so it's possible the pump and injectors took a knock. Nobody can tell you that from a forum, it has to be inspected. Tash's cousin's R40 000 is what it costs when the whole injection system is gone, and you're not there until someone has actually looked. If the pump and injectors are fine, it's drain the tank, flush the lines, new fuel filter and bleed it, usually R2 500 to R4 500. I can't promise you a total tonight.

What to do now:

1. Key out. Leave it out.
2. Tow it, don't drive it one metre. Check your insurance policy before you pay a tow guy cash, as most include a roadside tow.
3. I'm open tomorrow 7 till 12. Get it to me and my guy Thabo can drain it first thing, once we've checked the pump and injectors. DM me for the address.
4. Borrow a bakkie for the cake and the sound system anyway. Don't plan your wedding round a drained tank.

And you're in good company. One customer of mine did this twice in the same year, at the same garage. We made him a sticker for the fuel flap. My first year as an apprentice, 1995, I put diesel in the boss's Golf. He still tells it at every braai. You'll be telling this one at your anniversaries.

Congrats on the wedding, Sizwe. Go get married, we'll sort the bakkie. Just don't touch that key.
